sentences.text: Having
heard both sides, perused the entire material on record.
3. The claimants have filed two claim petitions vide O.P.Nos.303 of 1998 and 304 of 1998.

O.P.No.303 of 1998 is filed seeking compensation under no fault liability for fixing a sum of Rs.50,000/- and O.P.No.304 of 1998 is filed under Section 166(1)(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, seeking compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.

The tribunal has observed that as the tribunal is deciding main O.P. i.e., O.P.No.304 of 1998 is deciding, there is no need to decide O.P.No.303 of 1998, which is filed under no fault liability and observed that even if the said amount is awarded, the same shall has to be reduced from the compensation awarded in the main O.P. i.e., O.P.No.304 of 1998.
Hence, no amount was granted in O.P.No.303 of 1998.
Coming to O.P.No.304 of 1998, the Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.1,64,000/-.

When this matter came up on 19.07.2023, under the caption "for orders" as there was no representation for the Insurance Company, this Court has appointed Sri Ch.Venkata Narayana,
learned counsel to represent the Insurance Company.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the respondents ought to have disclosed the fact of receiving compensation under the workmen compensation, which amounts to playing fraud on the Court.
The Tribunal went wrong in believing the evidence of PW-2 who alleged to have seen the occurrence, but failed for the reasons of his presence at the work spot.
When he is an employee, granting compensation of Rs.1,64,000/-is exorbitant.
The Insurance Company has come up for the first time before this Court with such plea stating that the amounts were received under the Workmen Compensation Act.
He also submits that counter has been filed before the Court below stating that the claimant drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and the claim is excessive.

sentences.text: Even in the course of arguments also no such arguments were advanced by the Insurance Company.

Hence, the Tribunal has rightly held that there is negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle LK, J MACMA_4057_2008 and granted compensation, as no grounds are made out by the Insurance Company, the tribunal has dismissed the appeal.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that Court below considering all the aspects has granted the compensation and no grounds are made out seeking interference with the well reasoned order passed by the Tribunal.
8. Accordingly, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
9. As this Court has appointed Sri Ch. Venkata Narayana, learned counsel to represent the Insurance Company, his fee is fixed at Rs.15,000/- apart from expenses of Rs.3,000/- i.e., total Rs.18,000/-.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
___________________________ LALITHA KANNEGANTI, J Date: 21.07.2023 Smk/Vsl LK,
J MACMA_4057_2008 THE HON'BLE SMT.
